mechanism_basis: The fly rescue used mitochondrial chaperones Hsp60/Hsp60c, whereas arimoclomol is described experimentally as a context-dependent HSP70/heat-shock-response co-inducer and its labeled clinical mechanism in NPC is unknown.
public_result_boundary: Zero of 12 evaluable modules passed BH q<=0.10. Four Hsp70-family paralogs rose in one fly dataset, but this is one correlated family signal, not independent replication or proteostasis-module support; folding/proteasome direction reversed when blocks 4 or 6 were omitted.
cns_pediatric_regulatory_basis: Current US approval is only with miglustat for neurological manifestations of NPC in adults and children age 2 years and older. The label reports dose-dependent CSF concentrations, giving stronger neural exposure plausibility than the other non-mTOR probes; neither fact establishes MVA efficacy.
hazard_contradiction: HSF1 overexpression has been shown to tolerate aneuploidy in human cells, and HSF1 activation can support cancer-cell drug resistance. Amplifying a cytoprotective stress response could therefore preserve CIN clones or chemotherapy-exposed cells; this is pathway-level concern, not evidence that arimoclomol causes cancer.
counterevidence: The current label reports no tumor increase in rat and rasH2-mouse carcinogenicity studies at exposures above the labeled human exposure; this does not test MVA-associated clone persistence or chemotherapy resistance. A randomized phase 3 ALS trial found no efficacy benefit, and its safety data suggested that a higher dose would not have been tolerated; ALS is not MVA, but the negative trial limits broad neuroprotective extrapolation.
falsifier: Reject for benefit failure if verified HSF1/HSP70 engagement does not improve neural identity/output or if benefit is absent at either locked dose; reject for safety only on a prespecified replicated adverse signal or an interval supporting calibrated material harm. A safety interval crossing its margin is indeterminate/no-advance, not evidence of harm.
advance_rule: Eligible only as arimoclomol versus vehicle after the exact three-endpoint/two-dose rule, orthogonal model confirmation, and every safety gate pass; never as a treatment nominee. Direct ranking versus elamipretide is secondary unless separately powered.

mechanism_basis: The label identifies elamipretide as a mitochondrial cardiolipin binder. This is adjacent to the fly mitochondrial-dysfunction mechanism and Hsp60/Hsp60c and Sod2/GTPx-1 genetic rescues, but elamipretide itself was not tested in the SAC/CIN model.
public_result_boundary: Zero of 12 evaluable modules passed BH q<=0.10; mitochondrial_energy had q=0.734. Public transcriptomics therefore provides no mitochondrial-module support for elamipretide.
cns_pediatric_regulatory_basis: Current accelerated US approval is only to improve muscle strength in Barth syndrome in adult and pediatric patients weighing at least 30 kg, with confirmatory evidence still required. Neural evidence is preclinical; no human MVA or human CNS target-engagement evidence was found.
hazard_contradiction: Elamipretide restored invasion in ACADM-knockdown breast-cancer cells and protected osteosarcoma cells from ROS/ER-stress-mediated killing in vitro. These direct candidate-specific contradictions trigger mandatory invasion, clone-persistence, and chemotherapy-sensitization gates.
counterevidence: The label reports negative genotoxicity assays, but carcinogenicity studies were not conducted. A phase 3 trial in primary mitochondrial myopathy did not improve its two primary outcomes, further limiting efficacy extrapolation.
falsifier: Reject for benefit failure if mitochondrial metrics improve without neural output or if benefit is absent at either locked dose; reject for safety only on a prespecified replicated adverse signal or an interval supporting calibrated material harm. A safety interval crossing its margin is indeterminate/no-advance, not evidence of harm.
advance_rule: Eligible only as elamipretide versus vehicle after the exact three-endpoint/two-dose rule, orthogonal model confirmation, and every safety gate pass. It need not defeat arimoclomol; direct ranking is secondary unless separately powered.

mechanism_basis: Sirolimus is rapamycin, the compound fed in the published fly SAC/CIN model. It increased the number of aneuploid neural stem cells but did not rescue differentiated progeny or brain size, making it the most direct mechanistic control and an already-demonstrated partial, uncoupled rescue.
public_result_boundary: Zero of 12 evaluable modules passed BH q<=0.10; autophagy_mitophagy had q=0.198 and is hypothesis-generating only. No transcriptomic nomination is permitted.
cns_pediatric_regulatory_basis: Current US approvals concern renal-transplant rejection prophylaxis from age 13 and lymphangioleiomyomatosis, not pediatric neurodevelopment or MVA. CNS translation is weak and systemic immunosuppression is material.
hazard_contradiction: The same-model result may represent persistence of aneuploid neural stem cells without restored function. The current label warns that immunosuppression can increase infection and lymphoma/other malignancy risk; only a prespecified replicated clone-persistence increase or interval supporting calibrated material harm is called a hard stop.
counterevidence: Sirolimus is anti-proliferative through mTOR and is approved for LAM, so tumor risk is context-dependent rather than uniformly pro-oncogenic.
falsifier: Classify the control as uncoupled/no-go if neural output remains uncoupled from neural-stem-cell count; call safety harm only on a prespecified replicated adverse signal or interval supporting calibrated material harm. A safety interval crossing its margin is indeterminate/no-advance, not evidence of harm.
advance_rule: Use only as a same-model assay-validity control; it is ineligible for advancement in the current candidate family.

mechanism_basis: Everolimus is a rapamycin analog that inhibits mTORC1, so it is a translational class comparator to the direct sirolimus/rapamycin fly experiment, not the tested intervention itself.
public_result_boundary: Zero of 12 evaluable modules passed BH q<=0.10; autophagy_mitophagy had q=0.198 and is not support. It cannot outrank the null primary analysis.
cns_pediatric_regulatory_basis: Current US labels include TSC-associated SEGA from age 1 and TSC-associated seizures from age 2, providing substantial pediatric CNS and rare-disease experience in a different mechanism and indication.
hazard_contradiction: Class inference from the fly result raises concern that mTOR inhibition could preserve aneuploid stem cells without restoring output. Autophagy can mediate resistance to everolimus in cancer models, and immunosuppression/infection plus anti-proliferative effects are relevant to a growing brain.
counterevidence: Everolimus is also an approved antineoplastic agent; its label describes reduced proliferation/angiogenesis and reports no oncogenic signal in two-year rodent studies. This lowers, but does not eliminate, CIN-specific concern.
falsifier: Classify as no-go if it reproduces sirolimus uncoupling or impairs normal progenitor growth; call safety harm only on a prespecified replicated adverse signal or interval supporting calibrated material harm. A safety interval crossing its margin is indeterminate/no-advance, not evidence of harm.
advance_rule: Use only as an mTOR-class control after sirolimus validates the assay; it is ineligible for advancement in the current family and cannot outrank the direct same-compound result or module-level null.

mechanism_basis: The fly study showed full brain-size rescue with genetic ROS-scavenger overexpression (Sod2 or GTPx-1). NAC restores glutathione and is a pharmacologic redox probe, but it is not those enzymes and was not tested in the SAC/CIN model.
public_result_boundary: Zero of 12 evaluable modules passed BH q<=0.10; oxidative_stress had q=0.772, and its direction reversed when blocks 4 or 6 were omitted. GstE8 upregulation is one gene-level signal, not pathway replication.
cns_pediatric_regulatory_basis: Current US approval is an intravenous antidote for acetaminophen overdose in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 5 kg, not chronic antioxidant treatment or MVA. Human CSF exposure after oral administration supports neural testability but not efficacy.
hazard_contradiction: NAC accelerated lung-tumor progression and melanoma metastasis in mouse models, promoted intestinal-tumor progression in another model, and attenuated ROS-dependent osteosarcoma killing in vitro. These repeated candidate-specific contradictions make it a control, not a lead.
counterevidence: Older primary studies reported anti-invasive and anti-metastatic effects in other tumor contexts, confirming that NAC oncology effects are context-dependent. The label states that long-term carcinogenicity studies were not performed.
falsifier: Classify as a failed redox control if lowering ROS does not restore neural output; call safety harm only on a prespecified replicated adverse signal or interval supporting calibrated material harm. A safety interval crossing its margin is indeterminate/no-advance, not evidence of harm.
advance_rule: Use only as a ROS-direction and assay-response control; it is ineligible for advancement in the current family.
